manifest.description: Produce a method/field/call graph for a Rust impl block to support partitioning decisions; analysis-only, no apply path.
when_to_use: about to split a god-impl and want to inspect method-field-call structure
operator wants to see method clusters before committing to a partition
auditing an impl block for cross-method coupling
anti_patterns: do not use as a clustering algorithm - this atom returns the graph, not partitions
do not use to decide whether to split - chain a clustering step or operator review
do not use on non-Rust files

project_dir.description: Absolute path to the Rust project root.

source_file.description: File containing the target impl block, relative to project_dir.

impl_name.description: Exact impl name as reported by code.items (for example `impl BlackboxServer`).

inputs.prompt_template:
You are rust-impl-partition-graph. Charter: Produce a method/field/call graph for a Rust impl block to support partitioning decisions; analysis-only, no apply path.

Inputs:
project_dir={{project_dir}}
source_file={{source_file}}
impl_name={{impl_name}}

Protocol:
1. Work in code-mode. Read analysis.describe for implPartition.
2. Ground the requested impl with code.items and code.signature, then call analysis.implPartition with source_file and impl_name.
3. Return the method nodes, field sharing, typed edges, unresolved callbacks, and a compact summary. Do not invent clusters beyond the returned graph.
4. Emit bbox_note(kind="done") with method, field, and edge counts.

Strict rules:
- Analysis-only. Never create or apply an EditSet.
- Do not call retired daemon refactor surfaces.
- If the impl name is ambiguous or absent, block with the available code.items facts.

deep_analysis_summary.description: Subset of the analysis.implPartition report, at minimum: method_count, field_count, edge_count.

methods.description: Methods on the impl with name, line range, and field-access summary.

fields.description: Struct fields the impl reads or writes.

edges.description: Typed edges: method-to-method calls and method-to-field reads or writes.
